description_en: Both the Vajrayoginī and Jogeśvara temples are believed to be built on a single rock without a proper foundation.In 2000/2001 CE, the Friends of Sankhu, a local organization, repurposed copper sheets from the Vajrayoginī temple to cover the Jogeśvara temple(B. Shrestha2012, p. 417).Previously, the lower roof was clad with corrugated iron sheets(B. Shrestha2012, p. 417).The entrance to the sanctum is covered with gilded sheets along with atoraṇaabove. A person named Kulavīrasiṃha had donated the decorative covering during the reign of King Surendra in 1878 CE (NS 998). Thetoraṇaabove the main entrance has a figure of Mahā-amitābha (tantric form of Amitābha) at the centre flanked by Prajñāpāramitā and Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara.[1]Inside the sanctum, acaityais enshrined as the main deity. A large stone is covered with silver sheets in the shape of a dome topped withharmikāandtrayodaśabhuvanaspire to give it the shape of acaitya. The Jogeśvara Temple is, therefore, a unique temple of Nepal as it has acaityaas its main deity. This Caitya is known with multiple names. It is believed to be self-originated and hence referred to as Svayambhū Caitya. The Temple also gets its name from the Caitya known as Jogeśvara Caitya named after Jogadeva Vajrācārya, who founded the town of Sankhu (D. Sharma and T. Shrestha2016, p. 256). It is also revered as Dhavala Caitya by the locals, who believe that Jogeśvara is the husband of Hyāũkhvāḥmāju (Vajrayoginī) and the father of Siṃhinī and Vyāghriṇī (B. Shrestha2012, p. 417). Some locals claim that there is aśivaliṅgainside the Caitya, however the Vajrācārya priests of the Temple refute the claim (B. Shrestha2012, p. 417). Hindus worship this Caitya as aśivaliṅgain the form of Jogeśvara Mahādeva and is enlisted as the 32nd of the 64śivaliṅgas in Nepal. Hindu scriptures state that a person will be absolved of all his sins and will attain a place at the abode of Śiva if he takes a bath here on the 8th of the bright fortnight of Phālguna and the 9th of the dark fortnight of Āśvina (H. Jośī2058, p. 396). It is a Licchavi Caitya but does not appear to belong to the period before the 7th century (Slusser1982, p. 150).Although the Jogeśvara Mandira appears to be a two-story temple from the outside, it is, in reality, a Buddhist monastery widely known as Gũ Bāhāḥ (Gũ Vihāra). The Caitya itself is thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥof the Bāhāḥ.Gũis a vernacular term meaning ‘forest’. The name ‘Gũ Bāhāḥ’ attributes to its location within the forest of a hillock named Maṇicūḍa. It is the foremost Buddhist monastery of the Kathmandu Valley. The establishment of this monastery also marks the rise of the Buddhist civilization in Nepālamaṇḍala (Vajrācārya et alNS 1120, p. 10). All the Vajrācāryas from the Kathmandu Valley are said to have migrated from the Gũ Bāhāḥ.[3]Therefore, the Caitya at Gũ Bāhāḥ is the main lineage deity of the Vajrācāryas. It also functions as thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥat the time of performing the initiation of boys at the Gũ Bāhāḥ.D. Vajrācārya2030, p. 510 opines that this monastery dates back to the Kirant period. An inscription of Aṃśuvarman at Hā̃ḍigāũ, Kathmandu states that the Gũ Vihāra was allocated a grant of 6purāṇas 2paṇas from the state equal to the grants for Paśupati and Cā̃gunārāyaṇa in 608 CE i.e., Mānadeva Era 32 (D. Vajrācārya2030, p. 320-321). This is the earliest historical record that has a clear mention of the Gũ Vihāra (Jogeśvara Mandira). This tiered Temple/Monastery was once constructed in theśikharastyle as well. An entry of an annal dated the 1st of the dark fortnight of Māgha in 1689 CE (NS 809) refers to it as a two-tier temple (T. Siṃha1136, p. 15, folio 23A). On the 13th of the bright fortnight of Phālguna in 1689 CE (NS 809), King Bhūpālendra Malla got the two-tiered Temple dismantled and got a door installed for constructing aśikhara-style (granthakūṭa) temple (T. Siṃha1136, p. 15, folio 23A). A few years later, theśikhara-style Temple constructed at the orders of Bhūpālendra Malla was again rebuilt as a two-tiered Temple and a finial was installed on the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Phālguna in 1727 CE (NS 847) (T. Siṃha1136, p. 28, folio 46A). Another record shows that the Temple was renovated and aguthiwas formed by donating plots of land by a person named Bhikhvādhana along with his wife Mayajudhaṃ and other family members in 1849 CE (NS 969). Although the Temple did not collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, it suffered severe damages and stood on wooden supports. The Department of Archaeology rebuilt both the Vajrayoginī and Jogeśvara Temples at a total cost of NRs. 59.2 million.Footnotes^Slusser1982, p. 278 has erroneously identified the central image of thetoraṇaas Mahāmayūrī, one of thepañcarakṣādeities, and that the temple was dedicated to her.Gutschow2011, p. 453 andD. Sharma and T. Shrestha2016, p. 260 have also followed Slusser’s assertion.^Vajrācāryas are commonly referred to asgubhāju. Some interpret the termgubhājuas someone who hails from Gũ Bāhāḥ. Linguistically, however, it is clear that the termgubhājucomes from the Sanskrit termgurubhaṭṭāraka.
description_ne: साँखुको गुँ बाहाः परिसरमा वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर (SKH0500) को पूर्वमा जोगेश्वर मन्दिर रहेको छ । पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यो मन्दिर दुई तलाको छ । वज्रयोगिनी र जोगेश्वर दुबै मन्दिरको जग छैन, दुबै मन्दिर एउटै सिंगो ढुङ्गामाथि बनाइएको मानिन्छ । छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखिको छ । मन्दिरका दुबै छानामा तामाको पाता राखिएको छ ।[1]मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका र तोरणमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छ । नेसं ९९८ (सन् १८७८) मा राजा सुरेन्द्रको राज्यकालमा कुलवीरसिंहले सुवर्ण लेपित प्रवेशद्वार र तोरण चढाएका थिए । प्रवेशद्वारको माथि रहेको तोरणको बीचमा महाअमिताभ राखी दायाँबायाँ प्रज्ञापारमिता र षडक्षरी लोकेश्वर राखिएका छन् ।[2]गर्भगृहभित्र चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । ठूलो ढुङ्गालाई चाँदीको पाताले छोपी हर्मिका र भुवनहरू राखी चैत्य निर्माण गरिएको छ । चैत्यलाई भित्र राखी मन्दिर बनाइएकोले यसलाई नेपालकै विशिष्ट मन्दिर मान्न सकिन्छ । यो चैत्यलाई आफै उत्पन्न भएको मानेर स्वयम्भू चैत्य पनि भनिन्छ । साँखुको निर्माण गर्ने जोगदेव वज्राचार्यको नाममा चैत्यलाई जोगेश्वर चैत्य पनि भनिन्छ (D. Sharma and T. Shrestha2016, p. 256) । जोगेश्वर चैत्य राखिएको मन्दिर हुनाले नै जोगेश्वर मन्दिर भनिएको हो । यस चैत्यलाईधवल चैत्यपनि भनिन्छ । साँखुवासीहरू जोगेश्वरलाई ह्याउँख्वाःमाजु (वज्रयोगिनी) को श्रीमान् र सिंहिनी-व्याघ्रिनीको बुबा मानेर पूजा गर्छन् (B. Shrestha2012, p. 417) । केही मानिसहरू चैत्यभित्र शिवलिङ्ग रहेको र पछि चैत्यले शिवलिङ्गलाई छोपेको भनी दावी गर्छन् तर वज्राचार्य पूजारीहरू त्यसको खण्डन गर्छन् (B. Shrestha2012, p. 417) । हिन्दू धर्मावलम्बीहरू यस चैत्यलाई शिवलिङ्ग मानेर पूजा गर्छन् । नेपालका ६४ शिवलिङ्गमध्ये यसलाई ३२ औं क्रममा राखेर जोगेश्वर महादेवको रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ । फागुन शुक्ल ८ र आश्विन कृष्ण ९ को दिनमा यहाँ आएर स्नान गरेमा सबै पाप नाश भएर शिवलोकमा बास हुन्छ भन्ने कुरा ग्रन्थमा लेखिएको छ (H. Jośī2058, p. 396) । यो चैत्य लिच्छविकालीन हो तर सातौं शताब्दीभन्दा अगाडिको देखिँदैन (Slusser1982, p. 150) ।बाहिरबाट हेर्दा यो दुई तले मन्दिर हो, तर वास्तवमा यो बाहाः हो । यसलाई गुँ बाहाः (गुँ विहार) भनिन्छ । मन्दिरभित्र रहेको चैत्य नै बाहाःकोक्वाःपाःद्यःहुन् । नेवारीमागुँको अर्थ जंगल हो । मणिचूड पर्वतको जंगलमा रहेको बाहाः हुनाले यसलाई गुँ बाहाः भनिएको हो । काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा रहेका सबै विहारभन्दा यो पुरानो विहार हो । जुन दिन गुँ विहारको स्थापना भयो त्यस दिनदेखि नेपाल मण्डलमा बौद्ध सभ्यताको उदय भएको मानिन्छ (Vajrācārya et alNS 1120, p. 10) । काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा रहेका जति पनि वज्राचार्य छन् ती सबै गुँ बाहाःबाटै बसाइँसराइ गरेका थिए ।[3]त्यसैले वज्राचार्यहरूको मूल कुलदेवता गुँ बाहाःमा रहेको चैत्य नै हो । गुँ बाहाःमा व्रतबन्ध गर्दा चैत्यलाई नै क्वाःपाःद्यः मानी संस्कार सम्पन्न गरिन्छ ।यो बाहाःको निर्माणबारे ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण पाइएको छैन ।D. Vajrācārya(2030, p. 510) ले यस बाहाःलाई किरातकालीन मानेका छन् । हाँडिगाउँको अंशुवर्माको मासं ३२ (सन् ६०८) को अभिलेखमा पशुपतिनाथ, चाँगुनारायण सरह नै गुँ विहारलाई पनि राज्यको तर्फबाट ६ पुराण २ पण अनुदानको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ (D. Vajrācārya2030, 320-321) । गुँ विहार (जोगेश्वर मन्दिर) उल्लेख गरिएको यो नै सबैभन्दा पुरानो प्रमाण हो । अहिले यो दुई तले मन्दिर भएपनि एकताका शिखरकूट मन्दिरको रूपमा पनि बनाइएको थियो । नेसं ८०९ माघ कृष्ण प्रतिपदा (सन् १६८९) को घटना टिपोटमा यो मन्दिरलाई दुई तले मन्दिर नै भनिएको छ (T. Siṃha1136, p. 15, folio 23A) । नेसं ८०९ फागुन शुक्ल १३ (सन् १६८९) मा राजा भूपालेन्द्र मल्लले शिखरकूट (ग्रन्थकूट) मन्दिर बनाउनको लागि चैत्य रहेको दुई तले मन्दिरलाई भत्काएर विधिपूर्वक द्वार स्थापना गरेका थिए (T. Siṃha1136, p. 15, folio 23A) । केही वर्षपछि नेसं ८४७ फागुन शुक्ल ३ (सन् १७२७) मा भूपालेन्द्र मल्लले बनाएको जोगेश्वरको शिखरकूट मन्दिरको ठाउँमा पुनः दुई तले मन्दिर बनाएर गजूर चढाइएको थियो (T. Siṃha1136, p. 28, folio 46A) । नेसं ९६९ (सन् १८४९) मा भिख्वाधनले श्रीमती मयजुधं र परिवारका अन्य सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी जग्गा गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा क्षति पुगेको थियो । मन्दिर नभत्केपनि धेरै ठाउँमा चर्केको थियो र मन्दिर नभत्कियोस् भनेर टेको राख्नुपरेको थियो । भूकम्पले क्षति पुगेको वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर र जोगेश्वर मन्दिरको पुरातत्व विभागबाट एकैपल्ट पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा दुबै मन्दिरको गरी जम्मा ५ करोड ९२ लाख खर्च भएको थियो । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री योगेश भट्टराईले मन्दिरको उद्घाटन गरेका थिए ।गुँ बाहाः (जोगेश्वर मन्दिर) मा वज्राचार्य र बुद्धाचार्य (शाक्य) को पाँचवटा खलक (मूल, इल, छ्वाक, क्वचि, ईथु) को संयुक्त संघ रहेको छ । उनीहरूले एक-एक हप्ताको पालो मिलाएर बाहाःमा नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । बाहाःमा दिनको चारपल्ट पूजा गर्नुपर्छ । बिहानको नित्यपूजापछि १० बजे, २ बजे र ५ बजे पनि पूजा गर्नुपर्छ । बिहानको प्रथम पूजा र २ बजेको पूजामा मात्र उत्तर दिशामा फर्केरधर्मगण्डीबजाइन्छ । बाहाःमा नित्यपूजा गर्दा वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरका देवीदेवताहरू र म्हासुख्वाःमाजु द्यःछेँ (SKH0550) मा पनि नित्यपूजा गर्छन् । एक हप्तासम्म द्यःपाःलाः घर जान पाउँदैन, म्हासुख्वाःमाजु द्यःछेँमा नै सुत्नुपर्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमादेखि आठ दिनसम्म वज्रयोगिनीको जात्रा मनाइन्छ । म्हासुख्वाःमाजु द्यःछेँमा जोगेश्वर मन्दिरभित्र रहेको स्वयम्भूको प्रतिरूप चैत्य बनाएर स्थापना गरिएको छ । जात्राको चौथो दिन वैशाख कृष्ण ३ मा म्हासुख्वाःमाजु, सिंघिनी, व्याघ्रिनी सँगै म्हासुख्वाःमाजु द्यःछेँमा राखिएको स्वयम्भू चैत्यलाई पनि खटमा राखेर साँखु परिक्रमा गराइन्छ । वैशाख कृष्ण ७ अन्य देवीदेवतासँगै स्वयम्भू चैत्यलाई पनि म्हासुख्वाःमाजु द्यःछेँमा ल्याएर पूर्ववत् स्थानमा विधिपूर्वक स्थापना गरिन्छ ।[1]पहिले तल्लो छानामा जस्तापाता राखिएको थियो (Locke1985, p. 467) । पछि फ्रेण्ड्स अफ् साँखुले वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा सन् २०००/२००१ तिर वज्रयोगिनीको छानामा राखिएको तामाको पातालाई पुनः प्रयोग गरी जोगेश्वर मन्दिरमा राखिएको थियो (B. Shrestha2012, p. 417) ।[2]Slusser(1982, p. 278) ले महाअमिताभलाई पञ्चरक्षादेवी मध्येका महामयूरी ठानेर मन्दिर नै महामयूरीलाई समर्पित गरी बनाइएको भनेका छन् ।Gutschow(2011, p. 453) रD. Sharma and T. Shrestha(2016, p. 260) ले पनि उनलाई नै पछ्याएका छन् ।[3]वज्राचार्यलाई नेवारीमागुभाजुभनिन्छ । गुँ बाहाःबाट आएका हुनाले वज्राचार्यहरूलाईगुभाजुभनिएको हो भन्ने पनि सुनिन्छ । तर भाषावैज्ञानिक रूपले संस्कृत शब्दगुरुभट्टारकजुबाट गुभाजु आएको हो भन्ने कुरा सिद्ध भइसकेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Earliest reference to Jogeśvara Mandira recording a land endowment
historical_events.event_description: An inscription of Aṃśuvarman at Hā̃ḍigāũ, Kathmandu, records that the Gũ Vihāra (Jogeśvara Mandira) was allocated a grant of 6purāṇas 2paṇas from the state equal to the grants for Paśupati and Cā̃gunārāyaṇa. This is the earliest historical record that has a clear mention of the Gũ Vihāra.
Mayā Bhāro of Sankhu commissioned the renovation of the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Drop of blood on the ring of Svayambhū Caitya and special ritual worship
historical_events.event_description: Some drops of blood were seen on thetrayodaśabhuvanaof the Svayambhū Caitya inside the Jogeśvara Temple complex. The king was informed about the incident and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed.

The temple was subjected to a break-in, resulting in the theft of three garlands made of precious metal, two copper water jars, and one plate. Subsequent to the incident, special rituals were conducted to restore auspiciousness.

historical_events.event_name: Temporarily removing the spirit of the temple
historical_events.event_description: The spirtit (essence) was removed and the finial was brought down.

historical_events.event_name: Installing door to build new temple
historical_events.event_description: King Bhūpālendra Malla got the two-tiered Temple dismantled and got a door installed for constructing aśikhara-style (granthakūṭa) temple.

historical_events.event_name: Offering pinnacle to newly constructed two storied temple
historical_events.event_description: Theśikhara-style temple constructed at the orders of Bhūpālendra Malla was rebuilt as a two-tiered temple and a finial was installed.
Bhavānīsiṃha and Govarddhanasiṃha from Kela Ṭola, Kathmandu, commissioned the construction of a rest-house (dharmaśālā). However, the specific rest-house mentioned in the inscription remains unclear.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the Temple and endowment of land
historical_events.event_description: Bhikhvādhana, along with his wife Mayajudhaṃ and other family members, got the Temple renovated and formed aguthiby donating some plots of land.
During the reign of King Surendra, Kulavīrasiṃha generously donated the decorative covering made of gilded sheets for the entrance to the sanctum, along with thetoraṇapositioned above it.
A donor from Calākhu Ṭola of Sankhu undertook the construction of thecaityalocated to the north of the Jogeśvara Temple complex.

historical_events.event_name: Offering a patāḥ to the temple
historical_events.event_description: Pañcavīrasiṃha Tulādhara and his family members made an offering of apatāḥto the temple in remembrance of their deceased family members.
Although the Temple did not collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, it suffered severe damages and stood on wooden supports.
The Department of Archaeology rebuilt both Vajrayoginī and Jogeśvara Temples at a total cost of NRs. 59.2 million.
